newsitem.title: UK: Southern Air says no plans for public flotation.
newsitem.headline: Southern Air says no plans for public flotation.

text.p: Privately-owned U.S. air cargo carrier Southern Air Transport might consider a public share flotation,"but there are no plans to do so," senior vice-president Asa Hemperley told a news briefing here.
"It is a possibility. It is one of different ways of funding, including (outside) equity investment, that we need to raise $20-30 million of capital," he added.
He was referring to the carrier's plans announced earlier to acquire a further four or five Boeing 747-200 freighters -- either by purchasing or long-term leasing -- by 2000.
Hemperley said that Southern was one of only a few cargo airlines still surviving that had emerged after World War Two "and has been owned by one individual for some 20 years."
